cohort: 300 hypertension patients aged above 25 attending the hypertension clinic of an Outpatient Department (OPD) in Udaipur, Rajasthan, India, excluding inpatients, those aged <25, with uncertain diagnoses, pregnant/lactating mothers, and patients subsequently admitted after OPD visits.
finding: The most prescribed antihypertensive drugs were Losartan (72%) and amlodipine (46%), with ARBs being the most prescribed drug class (79.3%), followed by CCBs (46.6%), and the majority of patients received a combination of two or three drugs.
